## M2.2 bond-output recognition: which chain outputs count as bonds

**This accounts for 2 of the 5 that is missing for bond recognition.**

What makes an on-chain output a bond, per the spec, and where each rule stood:

  R1  the output is P2TR (5A.3B)                       MISSING - built here
  R2  the transaction commits to H(advertisement)      already in (RESOLVE)
  R3  the advertisement names THIS outpoint (5A.1)     MISSING - built here
  R4  a dust output pays BOND_MARKER (25.1)            BLOCKED, marker null
  R5  the output's script tree is 5A.3B's template     BLOCKED until spent
  R6  the advertisement signature (5A.3)               BLOCKED, no curve

### The measurement that opened the letter

  candidate at vout 0  ->  eligible: 1   ACCEPTED
  candidate at vout 1  ->  eligible: 1   ACCEPTED     <- the OP_RETURN
  advert says its bond is at vout 0

  vout 0   value 100000000   script 5120 7777...  (34 bytes, P2TR)
  vout 1   value 0           script 6a20 c37c...  (34 bytes, OP_RETURN)

The census checked the transaction and the commitment and never looked at the
OUTPUT. A zero-value OP_RETURN counted as somebody's bond. A publisher could
have pointed an entry at a change output instead and inflated its own weight,
and nothing in the package would have said no.

### After

  candidate at vout 0  ->  eligible: 1
  candidate at vout 1  ->  excluded at step `resolve`, "that output is not a
                           taproot output, so it is not the bond 5A.3B
                           describes", and the root differs

SCAN still finds the OP_RETURN and reports its height. That is right: step 1
answers where an outpoint is and whether it was spent, not what it is for.

### RECOGNITION IS NOT ENUMERATION, and that is the whole letter

"Is this output a bond?" is answerable from chain data. "Find me every bond"
is not, and will not be until BOND_MARKER is chosen: 25.1 exists because "a
P2TR output is a 32-byte key and looks like every other one", so without the
marker there is nothing to scan FOR. The two questions were one conjunct on
the working list and they are not one question.

### No branch is written for the marker

`recognizeBond` names the marker in `unchecked` and does not test for it. A
branch comparing against a value nobody has chosen cannot be tested, and
shipping an untested path that looks ready is the same fault as writing a
plausible address into `constants.js`. When the marker is chosen the branch is
written and tested then.

### Mutants: 16 planted, 16 killed, none retracted

Eight of the "accepts a non-bond" family and four of the "drops a real bond"
family, as required, plus four on the census wiring:

  any script is taproot / the shape is not checked / witness version ignored
    / program length ignored / any vout the advert did not name / another
    transaction's advert / an out-of-range vout / a body with no outpoint
  nothing is a taproot output / the self-reference is not read / the vout must
    differ / recognition always refuses
  the census does not recognise at all / it recognises the wrong output / the
    marker is dropped from what it cannot check / the value comes back wrong

All died first time. The negative cases are real script shapes - P2PKH,
P2WPKH, P2WSH, a 31-byte program, and OP_2 instead of OP_1 - not a fabricated
"not taproot" blob.

### 15's remaining park, restated marker-done vs still-curve

  finding which outputs are bonds   HALF MOVED. Recognition is in; enumeration
                                    still needs BOND_MARKER.
  the bond script template          HALF MOVED. The CLASS is read (witness v1,
                                    32-byte program); the three spend paths
                                    stay hidden until one is spent, which is
                                    why 5A.3B chose taproot.
  the advertisement signature       UNMOVED. Still the curve.

So after this letter 15 waits on BOND_MARKER for one thing only - enumerating
bonds from the chain without being told where to look - plus the template's
paths and the curve. Nothing else about it is blocked on the marker.

### Suites

protocol 331/331 (was 325), blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client 89/89, core 80/80,
money guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean. No wire format
moved: recognition reads outputs, it does not add a field, so no round id, no
census root and no vector changed.

### The hole the recognition letter left, found by asking whether anything was missing

`recognizeBond` returned the output's value and the census went on believing
the ENTRY's `bondSats`. Measured on a real bond funded at 60000 sats:

  entry claims         60000  ->  eligible, census bondSats=60000,  weight 1
  entry claims             1  ->  refused, under the floor
  entry claims  100000000000  ->  ELIGIBLE, census bondSats=100000000000,
                                  weight 2000000

A two-million-fold selection advantage bought with a lie, on an output the
chain says is worth 60000 sats. 5A.3 says exactly why this is not a detail:
"The bond is what makes identity expensive. Without it, a Sybil attacker
creates arbitrarily many nodes for free and buys arbitrarily many selection
chances - the flaw that made v4.4 unsafe." A bond that is asserted rather than
observed costs nothing. `encodeEntry` hashes `bondSats` into the leaf, so the
lie was committed into the census root as well.

Not parked, because nothing parks it: the value was already in hand from the
output. `resolveCensus` now takes `bond.valueSats`, and both the floor check
and the census entry carry it. After: every claim above gives eligible=1,
bondSats=60000, weight 1; and a claim of 100000000000 against an output funded
at 49999 is refused, with the refusal carrying 49999 rather than the claim.

The fixtures had to be FUNDED rather than asserted - a test that only claims
49999 measures nothing once the amount is read off the chain.

Mutants: 6 more planted, 6 killed. One survived at 0 red - `valueSats` read
from `outputs[0]` instead of `outputs[vout]` - because every fixture had its
bond at vout 0 with only an OP_RETURN beside it. A funding transaction that
pays a bond and returns change to another taproot address is ordinary, and then
the bond is not vout 0; tested now, and reading the first output reports
somebody else's money as the bond.

Running total for this letter: 22 mutants planted, 22 killed, none retracted.
protocol 331 -> 333.

### And the same defect in the OTHER door, the one the player walks through

Asked the question a second time and found `acceptAdvert` had the hole the
census had just lost. It checked that the declared `bondVout` EXISTED and never
what it was. Measured on a real, merkle-proven bond transaction whose
advertisement declares vout 1 as its bond:

  advert names vout 1 = the OP_RETURN, value 0, script 6a20
  acceptAdvert says ok = true, endpoint wss://attacker.example

A transaction with no bond in it at all, presented to a client as a bonded node
with a reachable endpoint. `blwp-client/src/directory.js` is the caller, so
this is 25.1's own path: step 2 is "which nodes count? Bitcoin: bond outputs",
step 4 reads the endpoint from that same transaction. A node with nothing at
stake was answering step 2.

Fixed by using the same `recognizeBond` the census uses - one rule, one place,
both doors - and `acceptAdvert` now hands back `bondVout`, `bondSats` from the
output, and the three rules it could not read, instead of only an endpoint.

Mutants: 7 more planted, 7 killed, all first time. Running total for the
letter: 29 planted, 29 killed, none retracted. protocol 333 -> 334.

The client bundle was rebuilt; `bundle.test.js` is the guard that would have
caught a stale one.

### Third audit of the recognition goal: every door listed, two candidates cleared

The first two audits each found a live defect, so this one was done by
enumeration rather than by memory. `grep -rn "bondVout\|bondSats\|bondTxid"`
over `protocol/src`, `blwp-node/src` and `blwp-client/src` gives four places
that touch a bond outpoint or its value:

  census.js  resolveCensus       recognises. Shape, named outpoint, and the
                                 amount off the output. Fixed two letters ago.
  chain.js   acceptAdvert        recognises. Fixed one letter ago; the door
                                 `blwp-client/src/directory.js` walks through.
  slash.js   slashHolds* (x6)    binds each proof to the outpoint the accused
                                 node's own advertisement declared. Already in.
  slash.js   slashDistribution   takes `bondSats` as an argument.

CLEARED, WITH THE REASON, so it is not rediscovered as a bug:

`slashDistribution` is arithmetic over an amount and has no transaction to
read. That is the difference from the census: the census WAS handed the
transaction and used the entry's claim anyway, and the claim went into the leaf
and became the canonical fact. Here the amount is not committed to anything -
`slashProofId` commits the bond OUTPOINT (`w.bytes32(p.bondTxid); w.u32(p.bond
Vout)`), so the value is a public fact anyone holding the chain can look up and
a wrong distribution is detectable by everyone. Measured: a caller-supplied
100000000000 on an output worth 60000 does distribute 100000000000, and that is
the caller lying to itself about a number the proof already pins down.

`blwp-client/src/bond.js` `provenBond` proves INCLUSION and never claims
recognition; its only in-tree consumer, `askForBond`, feeds `directory.js`,
which runs `acceptAdvert` - so recognition happens before anything is used. It
is exported from the bundle under a name that could invite a page author to
read `.ok` as "this is a bond". Recorded rather than renamed: a public export
is not churned on a hunch, and no caller is wrong today.

Nothing changed in this audit. Suites re-run to confirm: protocol 334/334,
blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client 89/89, core 80/80, money guard 12 files clean,
determinism guard 19 files clean.

### Fourth audit: an output worth nothing was a bond, and a zero floor threw

The third audit enumerated the doors by NAME. This one asked what the values
themselves can be, which the names do not show. Measured:

  a P2TR output funded with 0 sats
  a round naming bondMinSats 0n
  -> census eligible: 1, bondSats=0
  -> selectCommittee THREW: Error: bondMin must be positive

Two things wrong, both this goal's own subject.

AN OUTPUT HOLDING NOTHING IS NOT A BOND, whatever shape it is. 5A.3: "The bond
is what makes identity expensive. Without it, a Sybil attacker creates
arbitrarily many nodes for free and buys arbitrarily many selection chances -
the flaw that made v4.4 unsafe." A zero-value P2TR output costs its fee and
nothing else, so a census counting them is that flaw with extra steps.
`recognizeBond` refuses it now: "that output holds nothing, so there is no bond
at stake". One satoshi IS a bond, and a bad one - how small is too small is the
ROUND's floor, and a round may set it low; nothing may set it to none.

A ZERO FLOOR IS NOT A SMALL FLOOR. The weight is bond/floor, so zero is a
division by zero, and `weightOf` threw from underneath `selectCommittee` -
a caller that had only asked who was on the committee got a RangeError-shaped
surprise from two frames down, against this package's rule everywhere else that
a malformed round is a refusal with a reason. `selectCommittee` now refuses a
non-positive floor by name, beside its three other guards.

Mutants: 6 more planted, 6 killed - the value check deleted, tightened to 1n,
loosened to negative-only, and the floor guard deleted, loosened to bigint-only,
loosened to negative-only. Running total for the letter: 35 planted, 35 killed,
none retracted. protocol 334 -> 335.

Note for the next audit: the first three passes each looked at NAMES (which
doors, which identifiers). This one looked at VALUES (zero, one, negative). The
angle that has not been tried is TIME - a bond spent between census_height and
the tip, a bond funded in a reorg - and SCAN owns both of those.

## The time pass on bond recognition: measured, and only one case is a hole

Two cases, instrumented before any change.

### CASE A - unspent at census_height, spent between it and the tip

  no spend at all              -> eligible 1, amount 60000, committee 1
  spent at H+5 (after census)  -> eligible 1, amount 60000, committee 1
  spent at H itself            -> eligible 0, "already spent at the census height"
  spent at H-5 (before)        -> eligible 0, "already spent at the census height"

  recognizeBond on the spent output still says ok = true

NOT A HOLE, and correct on purpose. 5A.4 step 1 is "unspent AT census_height",
so a spend later is not this census's business: if it were, the census would
change as the chain grows and two participants asking at different tips would
get different committees. 5A.3 states the consequence itself: "Proven
misbehaviour removes a node the only objective way - by its bond being spent by
a slashing transaction, which makes the output no longer unspent AT THE NEXT
census_height." A node whose bond goes away mid-round is removed by the NEXT
census, not this one.

`recognizeBond` saying ok on a later-spent output is also right: it answers
about the output's shape and value and never about spends. The spend is SCAN's
conjunct and SCAN applies it.

Pinned with a test, because only the COUNT was pinned before - not the amount,
not the seat. A mutant then survived: "spent, unless it was funded here". Every
fixture funded its bond well before the census height, so a bond funded AND
spent in the same block was never tested. One transaction creating an output
and another spending it in the same block is ordinary Bitcoin, and such a bond
was never unspent at any height. Tested now.

### CASE B - funded in a block later reorged out

  chain that HAS the funding block   -> eligible 1, root f81f56739efc0317
  chain where it was reorged out     -> eligible 0, "no such outpoint at or
                                        before that height"
  roots differ: true

THE CENSUS FAITHFULLY REPORTS WHATEVER CHAIN IT IS HANDED, which is all it can
do: `deriveCensus` takes blocks shaped `{height, transactions}` - no header, no
proof of work, no block hash. It cannot tell a reorged block from a live one
because it is never shown anything that would say.

RECOGNITION IS NOT WRONG HERE. Which chain is the chain is 25.1's question, and
25.1 answers it with headers from several independent sources, most work
winning, plus a merkle proof per transaction. That machinery exists already -
`chainWork`, `mostWork`, `provesTransaction` in `chain.js`, and `headers.js`
and `bond.js` in the client - and it is not wired into SCAN's block input.
Wiring it is SCAN's letter, not this one, and it is not pulled in.

### Share

Of the two time cases: recognition is right on both, so **0 of the 2 is missing
from recognition**. One of the two - the reorg - is missing from SCAN's chain
view: **1 of the 2 belongs to SCAN**, and it is named here with its numbers
rather than fixed.

  identifiers  done (audits 1 and 2)
  values       done (audit 4: zero, one, negative)
  time         done (this pass: spend after the census, spend in the census

  NOT DONE     the chain view itself - who says which chain the blocks came

               signature, all three still parked where they were.

## M2.2 item 17: SCAN's chain view - the rule, the doors, and what the code does today

Measured before any product code, as instructed. No product code in this pass.

### The rule, quoted rather than guessed from the JS

5A.2, on what a census IS:

  "A node is in the census if and only if it has a bond output on Bitcoin,
   confirmed and unspent at `census_height`, that commits to its
   NodeAdvertisement."
  "The eligible set is therefore a pure function of THE CHAIN up to
   `census_height`. Two parties with the same chain compute the same census;
   disagreement about the census reduces to disagreement about Bitcoin, which
   is out of scope by assumption."

25.1, on which chain that is:

  "block headers        from several independent sources, MOST WORK WINS
                        80 bytes a block; under 4 MB for all of history"
  "A list provider can then OMIT but not FORGE, and omission is answered by
   asking a second one."
  "A client MUST verify every census entry against block headers it obtained
   independently. It MUST NOT take a census, a committee or an endpoint on the
   word of any API, including one operated by the same party that ships the
   client."

5A.4, on the browser's residual:

  "It verifies the census root by (a) following the block-header chain and
   checking Merkle inclusion of the bond transactions (SPV), and/or (b)
   querying several independent chain providers and requiring agreement."

So the rule to implement: the blocks a census is derived from must be tied to a
header chain that was mined, and where two chains compete the one with the most
work is the chain. `census_confirmations` is what makes a shallow reorg
harmless; it is not what decides which chain.

### Every door that decides "which chain", or silently assumes one

  census.js   scanCensus / deriveCensus   takes `blocks`, shaped {height,
                                          transactions}. NO header, no work,
                                          no block hash, no link to a
                                          previous block.            HOLE 1
  census.js   commitCensus,
              censusInputsId,
              censusRootMatchesRound      take `tipHeight`, a bare number.
                                                                     HOLE 2/3
  chain.js    chainWork, mostWork         IMPLEMENT the rule. Refuse a header
                                          that does not meet its target.
                                          The census never calls them.
  client      headers.js                  agreement across sources, uses
                                          chainWork. Client only.
  client      directory.js                mostWork/chainWork, for the
                                          ADVERTISEMENT path only.
  client      bond.js provenBond          re-checks chainWork for one bond
                                          proof. Client only.
  blwp-node   (nothing)                   the node has no chain view at all.

### Measured

CASE 1 - a reorg that REPLACES the census block

  chain A, bond present    -> eligible 1, root f81f56739efc0317
  chain B, bond replaced   -> eligible 0, "no such outpoint at or before that
                              height"
  was the derivation told which of A and B is the chain? NO.

Both derive cleanly. The census faithfully reports whichever list of blocks it
was handed, and has nothing to say about which one Bitcoin agrees with.

CASE 2 - a reorg AFTER census_height that does not touch the bond block

  without the later block          -> eligible 1, root f81f56739efc0317
  with a replaced block at H+3     -> eligible 1, root f81f56739efc0317
  same root: TRUE

CLEAN, and correct on purpose: blocks past `census_height` are skipped, so the
census does not move when the tip does. This is the case `census_confirmations`
exists for and it needs nothing.

CASE 3 - two competing tips with different work

  workOf(mainnet block 100000)     = 62209952899966
  chainWork([100000])              = ok true
  a header whose hash misses its
    target                         = ok false, "this header was not mined"
  mostWork picks the heavier       = works

The rule is implemented and correct in `chain.js`. The census cannot use it,
because `deriveCensus(blocks, { contract, tipHeight, candidates, resolve })`
has no argument that could carry a header.

AND THE TIP IS A FREE NUMBER:

  tipHeight  900010 -> eligible 1
  tipHeight  900000 -> eligible 1
  tipHeight  899999 -> eligible 1
  tipHeight  899000 -> eligible 0, "that output is -979 confirmations deep
                       where this round needs 6"
  tipHeight       0 -> eligible 0, "-899979 confirmations deep"
  tipHeight      -5 -> eligible 0, "-899984 confirmations deep"

A caller naming a low tip empties the census; one naming a high tip matures a
shallow bond. The comment in `census.js` says the tip "stays the caller's, and
that is not the same thing: the tip is OBSERVED chain state, not a rule."
Observed from WHAT? There is no chain in that function to observe it from, so
today the tip is asserted, not observed. That comment is half true and this
letter is what would make it true. A tip BELOW the census height is incoherent
by construction and is accepted, printing a negative depth instead of refusing.

### The three named holes

  1  the derivation is never shown a chain, so "most work wins" cannot be
     applied and two disagreeing chains both derive cleanly
  2  `tipHeight` is a caller number that decides who is deep enough
  3  a tip below `census_height` is accepted and yields a negative depth

Share: this is the whole remaining recognition-adjacent gap - which chain - not
a side path. Case 2 needs nothing.

### Suites, unchanged this pass

protocol 336/336, blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client 89/89, core 80/80. No product
code was written.

## M2.2 item 17, built: the census is a function of a chain

All three named holes, in the order they were named.

### 1. The derivation takes a chain, and most work wins

`deriveCensus(views, { contract, candidates, resolve })`. A view is
`{ blocks, firstHeight }`, each block `{ header, transactions }`, and
`chainViewOf` checks four things:

  mined      every header's hash meets the target it claims - `chainWork`,
             which already refused an unmined header and was never reached
             from the census
  linked     each header names the one before it
  contained  each block's transactions hash to the merkle root ITS OWN header
             commits to. Without this the headers are decoration: a real mined
             header with a fabricated transaction list would pass, which is
             the forgery 25.1 says a provider must not be able to commit.
  placed     heights are positional from `firstHeight`; the tip is the last
             block's height

`bestChainView` runs `mostWork`'s rule over competing views. A view that is
not a chain is not a competing answer, it is a bad source.

`blockMerkleRoot` was added to `tx.js` for the containment check. It DUPLICATES
on an odd level, which is the rule `merkleRoot` in `census.js` refuses to use -
because that one is ours to design and this one is a question about a block
that already exists. Validated against `merkleRootFromProof`, which the chain
suite proves against mainnet block 100000's real header.

Recognition (`recognizeBond`, `isTaprootOutput`, `BOND_UNCHECKED`) moved from
`census.js` to `chain.js`: both files need it, so it could not live in one and
be imported by the other. `census.js` re-exports it; the imports now run one
way only.

### 2 and 3. The tip is the chain's, and a short chain is refused

`tipHeight` is gone from every signature: `scanCensus`, `commitCensus`,
`censusInputsId`, `censusRootMatchesRound` and `deriveCensus` all take the
view. There is no argument left to pass a tip through.

A view claiming to be already checked is not believed on its word. The stamp
is a module-private Symbol whose VALUE pins `firstHeight:blocks.length:
tipHeight`, because a symbol alone was not enough: object spread copies
symbol-keyed properties, so `{ ...verified, tipHeight: 999999 }` would have
carried an honest stamp onto an invented tip. Found by writing the test, not
by a mutant.

### Measured, the same three cases

  CASE 1  reorg replacing the census block
    light chain without the bond   work 50
    heavy chain with the bond      work 1638425
    most work wins              -> eligible 1, from work 1638425
    heavier chain WITHOUT it    -> eligible 0, "no such outpoint at or before
                                   that height"
    the lighter chain is not a second census; it is not the chain.

  CASE 2  reorg after census_height, bond block untouched
    eligible 1 / 1, same root: TRUE.  Unchanged, as required.

  CASE 3  competing tips and unearned work
    workOf(mainnet block 100000) = 62209952899966   (unchanged)
    a header claiming mainnet's target, mined at the easy one:
      "that is not a chain: this header was not mined: its hash does not meet
       the target it claims"

  TIP BELOW census_height
    tip 899999 -> "that chain ends at height 899999, before this round's
                   census height 900000"
    tip 899990 -> the same, naming 899990
    tip 900000 -> eligible 1.  The census is the chain UP TO its height, so
                  the height itself is the boundary and it is fine.
    No negative depth is printed anywhere.

  THE TIP IS NOT A CALLER'S NUMBER
    caller says tipHeight 999999 -> census tip 900004, eligible 1
    caller says tipHeight      0 -> census tip 900004, eligible 1
    Before: 899999 gave one census and 899000 another.

### Mutants: 21 planted, 20 killed, 1 retracted with its reason

Killed: headers not checked for work (41 red), transactions need not match the
header (1), a block need not carry a header (2), the tip is the first height
(35), the tip is one too high (5), heights are all the first height (8), a tip
below the census allowed (2), the tip boundary excludes the census height (4),

not one still competes (1), derive ignores most work (1), a view need not say
where it starts (1), a caller's `ok` flag trusted (1), the stamp does not pin
the tip (1), the stamp is not compared (1), and four more.

RETRACTED, not counted: "the verified stamp is never set". Removing the stamp
makes `viewOrThrow` re-verify a view it has already verified - identical
behaviour, more work done. It is a no-op mutant and there is no assertion that
could kill it without asserting how many times a function is called.

trusted, because every test passed a real view and none passed a forged one to
the verifier doors; and the stamp did not pin the tip, which the spread case
above exposed.

### Audit of item 17 after it closed: the window, and the anchor

Two findings. The first is built; the second is named with its measurement and
the reason it cannot be built without choosing something nobody has chosen.

FOUND AND FIXED - A WINDOW IS NOT THE CHAIN. Measured, bond funded at H-20:

  view starts at 899980  -> ok, eligible 1, root 86353eb3...
  view starts at 899990  -> ok, eligible 0, root 00000000...,
                            "no such outpoint at or before that height"
  view starts at 900000  -> the same

A view beginning after a bond's funding block returned ok, an empty census, a
different root, and a REASON THAT CLAIMED SOMETHING IT HAD NOT LOOKED AT: "no
such outpoint at or before that height" is a statement about Bitcoin, and the
view had not reached back far enough to make it. 5A.2 says the eligible set is
"a pure function of the chain up to census_height" - two parties with the same
chain but different windows were quietly computing different censuses.

The window cannot be made unnecessary here: a bond can be funded at any height,
and enumerating them from the chain alone needs BOND_MARKER, which is parked.
So two things changed instead:

  - the refusal says what the view knows: "no such outpoint between height
    899990 and 900000, and this chain view does not reach further back".
  - `censusInputsId` commits `firstHeight`. A root taken over a short window is
    no longer interchangeable with one taken over a long window: the committed
    inputs differ, so `censusRootMatchesRound` refuses the swap with "not the
    census entries that were published". Measured in the test.

Mutants: 4 planted, 4 killed - the window not committed, the window committed
as the tip, a short view still claiming the chain, and the refusal not naming
the window.

NAMED, NOT BUILT - THE VIEW IS ANCHORED TO NOTHING. Measured:

  a wholly fabricated chain, mined at the easy target
  -> chainViewOf ok: true, work 50

`chainViewOf` accepts any self-consistent mined chain. Nothing ties its first
header to Bitcoin. The client does have an anchor - `directory.js` and
`headers.js` carry `BITCOIN_MAINNET_GENESIS` - and the census does not.

Work comparison is the defence that exists, and it is Bitcoin's own: a
fabricated chain at a real difficulty is not cheap. But 5A.4 names the other
one: a browser follows the header chain "far less from a checkpoint", and a
checkpoint is a VALUE SOMEBODY HAS TO CHOOSE - a height and a block hash, fixed
once, wrong forever if wrong. That is the same class as BOND_MARKER and
NETWORK_ID, and writing a plausible one into this tree would settle it by
accident. Genesis itself is in `chain.js` and is not a workable anchor for a
census at height 900000: requiring a view to reach block 0 is requiring 900,000
headers.

So this is a decision, not a task. It is recorded here rather than parked
silently, and it is the one thing about the chain view that this package
cannot finish on its own.

  protocol 343 -> 344. blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client 89/89, core 80/80, money
  guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean.

### Item 17 closed: both window boundaries, and the checkpoint left as a decision

THE WINDOW IS CLOSED, at both ends.

  a view ENDING before census_height    refused: "that chain ends at height
                                        899999, before this round's census
                                        height 900000"
  a view BEGINNING after census_height  refused: "that chain begins at height
                                        900001, after this round's census
                                        height 900000"
  a view that does not reach a bond     excluded with what it actually knows:
                                        "no such outpoint between height 899990
                                        and 900000, and this chain view does not
                                        reach further back"
  and the window is committed           `censusInputsId` covers `firstHeight`,
                                        so a short-window root does not pass
                                        under a long-window commitment

The second was found by auditing after the first: a view beginning after the
census height returned OK, an empty census, and "no such outpoint between
height 900001 and 900000" - a range that runs backwards, from a view that had
not seen one block the census is about. It is the mirror of the end rule, and
three fixtures had been quietly relying on it: they built a one-block view AT
the tip and called it the chain. They now span the census height, which is what
a view of a census has to do.

Mutants for this piece: 3 planted, 3 killed - the start rule deleted, its
boundary made exclusive, and its refusal made vague.

THE CHECKPOINT REMAINS A DECISION, NOT A TASK. `chainViewOf` still accepts any
self-consistent mined chain; a wholly fabricated one gives ok true, work 50.
Work comparison is the defence that exists and it is Bitcoin's own. 5A.4's
other answer is a checkpoint - a height and a block hash, fixed once, wrong
forever if wrong - which is the BOND_MARKER and NETWORK_ID class and is not
this package's to settle. Nothing plausible has been written into the census

### Audit of item 17, again: a tie decided the census, and a header could be emptied

Two findings, both built, neither needing a checkpoint.

A TIE ON WORK WAS DECIDED BY ARRIVAL ORDER. Measured:

  chain with the bond   work 50
  chain without it      work 50        tie
  offered [with, without] -> eligible 1, root 86353eb36de01ebf
  offered [without, with] -> eligible 0, root 0000000000000000
  same census either way:  FALSE

The same two inputs, two different censuses, chosen by the order a caller
happened to list them. 5A.2 says "two parties with the same chain compute the
same census", and that was not true of a tie. Worse, `mostWork`'s own comment
claimed "ties go to the first source offered, SO THE ANSWER DOES NOT DEPEND ON
THE ORDER" - which is self-contradictory; taking the first IS depending on it.

`mostWork` is left alone: taking the first of an equal pair is right for a NODE
choosing its own tip, which is Bitcoin's first-seen rule, and a node is allowed
to have been somewhere when a block arrived. A CENSUS is not allowed it, so
`bestChainView` breaks the tie on the TIP HASH - lower wins, arbitrarily but
fixed. The tip hash is the work itself, so nobody can choose it after the fact,
and both parties compute the same comparison from the same two chains.

A HEADER COULD BE EMPTIED OF THE TRANSACTIONS IT COMMITS TO. Measured:

  header at 899980 commits to root dce17b40350ec9a1
  the same block handed over with transactions: []  -> chainViewOf ok TRUE
  census from it -> eligible 0

The containment check was skipped when no transactions were offered, so a real
mined header could be presented with its block emptied and the bond in it
vanished. 25.1 lets a provider OMIT and says omission is answered by asking
another - but a view that CONTRADICTS ITS OWN HEADER is not omitting, it is
claiming a block Bitcoin does not have. Every real block has at least a
coinbase, so the only transaction list consistent with none is a merkle root of
zero, and that is now the rule.

### Mutants: 6 planted, 6 killed

One survived at 0 red: "the tie compares only the first byte". The fixtures
differed there, so a one-byte comparison gave the same answer and two tips
sharing a first byte would have fallen back to whoever spoke first.

The first attempt at that test ASSERTED NOTHING and I caught it before it was
committed: mining here is deterministic, so 400 "variants" built from identical
inputs were 400 copies of one chain, the search never found a pair, and the
assertion sat inside an `if` that never ran. The variants now differ by a
transaction in the first block, and the test fails loudly if the search comes
up empty rather than passing quietly.

### Suites

protocol 347/347 (345 before this pass), blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client 89/89,
core 80/80, money guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean.
Vectors unmoved. The checkpoint is still a decision and still not invented.

### Item 17 closed at the package boundary

Everything about the chain view that this package can decide is decided and
tested: the derivation takes a chain rather than a bag of blocks, headers must
be mined and linked and must commit to the transactions offered with them, a
block offered with none must have a header that says so, most work wins and a
tie is broken by the tip hash so the same two chains give one census in any
order, the tip is the chain's, and the view must straddle `census_height` with
the window it covered committed in `censusInputsId`.

What is left is not an engineering hole: `chainViewOf` is anchored to nothing,
so a wholly fabricated chain is a chain if it outweighs the real one. Work
comparison is the defence that exists and it is Bitcoin's own. 5A.4's other
answer is a checkpoint - a height and a block hash, fixed once and wrong
forever if wrong - which is the BOND_MARKER and NETWORK_ID class and is chosen
outside this package. Nothing plausible has been written for it.

The follow-up findings of this letter are recorded above: the arrival-order
tie, the emptied header, the mutant that compared only the first byte, and the
test that asserted inside an `if` that never ran.

### EXTERNAL REMAINDER: the chain anchor is Daniel's pick

Not a task, not a design exercise, and not this package's to attempt. The
census view is anchored to nothing, so a wholly fabricated chain is a chain if
it outweighs the real one; work comparison is the defence that exists and it is
Bitcoin's own. 5A.4's other answer is a checkpoint - a height and a block hash,
fixed once and wrong forever if wrong - which is the BOND_MARKER and NETWORK_ID
class. DANIEL CHOOSES IT. Nothing is designed for it here, no height, no block
hash and no genesis has been written into the census package, and no work on it
is queued.

Two facts this letter settled and that stay settled:

  a tie on work            broken by the tip hash, LOWER WINS, so two parties
                           with the same two chains compute the same census
                           whichever order the chains are offered. `mostWork`
                           keeps first-seen, which is right for a NODE choosing
                           its own tip; a census is not allowed it.
  an emptied header        a block handed over with no transactions while its
                           header commits to a merkle root is not omission
                           under 25.1 - it is a view that contradicts Bitcoin.
                           Refused unless that root is zero, which is the only
                           list consistent with none.

## M2.2 item 18, piece 1: a ghost is a picture from a transcript

0.9: "Other trucks are visible ghosts with no collision... Another player must
not be able to change my financial odds by ramming me, blocking a road,
pushing me, damaging me, drawing my enemies away, pulling enemies toward me,
sacrificing themselves for me, or colluding physically."

0.10: `financial_world(p) = deterministic_sim(RoundContract, map, player_seed,
player_inputs)`, and "Ghost snapshots are never inputs to this calculation."

### What was already true, measured before any code

  step(st, throttle, steer, brake, handbrake, practice)   sim.js:933
  one truck at one O_TRUCK block, TRUCK_WORDS = 13        state.js
  grep -i ghost over blwp-node/src, blwp-client/src,
    protocol/src                                          NOTHING
  the client has no notion of other players               4 modules, no roster

So nothing coupled, because other players did not exist in the client at all.
The hazard this letter manages is the coupling BUILDING ghosts would create.

### The frame

`TYPE_GHOST = 0x11`, `TAG.ghost`, 147 bytes fixed:

  u8  type | u16 version | b32 roundId | b32 entryId | b32 playerPubkey
  u32 tick | b32 inputChainHash | i32 x | i32 z | i32 heading

THREE WORDS OF TRUCK AND NO MORE. `T_X`, `T_Z`, `T_HEADING` draw a truck; the
core's other ten truck words are not carried, because each would be a claim
about somebody's run that a 5 Hz picture cannot prove and nothing needs in
order to render a ghost. Q16.16, unscaled at the boundary for the reason
`encodeInputBatch` gives.

A TYPE BYTE OF ITS OWN, so an InputBatch and a Ghost differ before a decoder
has read anything else. A mutant that stopped CHECKING that byte survived at
first: the test asserted the byte was written and never fed a mistyped frame
in. It dies now.

### The binding: a picture of a run somebody published inputs for

A node that simply announces coordinates paints competitors wherever it likes,
including competitors who never drove. Same fault as a payout table before
`payoutInputsId` and a census before `censusInputsId`, same fix: bind the thing
shown to the inputs it came from. The binding already existed on the wire -
§11's input chain - so a ghost names the head it was taken from, as a
checkpoint does. `ghostBinds(ghost, transcript, entry?)` refuses:

  a head no batch of that transcript hashes to   "taken from inputs nobody
                                                  published"
  GENESIS                                        "before any input went out,
                                                  so there is nothing it could
                                                  be a picture of"
  a tick those inputs do not cover               names the range: "at tick 6,
                                                  and the inputs it names cover
                                                  0 to 5"
  another round, another entry                   named separately
  a transcript whose chain is broken             "input chain is broken"
  a key that entry was not signed for            and with no entry offered, the
                                                 key is reported UNCHECKED
                                                 rather than believed

It does NOT say the truck was at x,z. Only a replay says that, and replay is
the objection path's job (§13A), not a 5 Hz frame's. What it says is that the
frame belongs to a run that happened.

### The guarantee is a missing parameter, and it is asserted as one

`packages/core/test/private-world.test.js` imports nothing from the protocol
package on purpose - a test that reached for a ghost type to prove a ghost
cannot arrive would be building the door it claims is absent. It asserts
`step.length === 6`, pins the parameter list verbatim, checks the state exports
name no second truck, and checks two runs of the same seed and inputs agree
word for word while different seeds do not.

Two mutants prove it bites: adding a seventh parameter to `step` named
`ghosts`, and one named `otherTruck`. Both die.

### Mutants: 14 planted, 14 killed, none retracted

Ghost frame (12): typed as an input batch, the type byte not checked, the key
not on the wire, the head not on the wire, the tick not on the wire, GENESIS
accepted, any head accepted, the tick range not checked, the range off by one,
the round not checked, the entry not checked, the entry's key not checked, the
unchecked key not reported, the transcript's chain not walked.

Core (2): `step` growing a seventh parameter, under two names.

Two survived at 0 red first and both were real gaps: nothing fed a mistyped
frame to the decoder, and nothing handed `ghostBinds` a transcript whose chain
was broken.

### Suites

protocol 353/353 (was 347), core 83/83 (was 80), blwp-node 70/70, blwp-client
89/89, money guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean. No wire
format that existed before moved: a new type byte and a new file, nothing
else, so no round id, census root or vector changed.

### What piece 1 is NOT

No Unity, no C#, no PhysX, no collider, no renderer, no lobby, no late join, no
fan-out, no interest management. No ghost array in the core state, and no wire
path that hands a ghost to the simulation - the missing parameter is the
guarantee. Pieces 2 to 4 stay on item 18.

## M2.2 item 18, piece 2: a picture carries no authority, and it is shed first

### What was measured before any code

The node's play socket dispatched on the first byte: checkpoint to its
handler, receipt to its handler, and EVERYTHING ELSE to `round.batch`. A ghost
was refused there - `decodeInputBatch` checks its own type byte - so the answer
was:

    decodeInputBatch(ghost) -> "not an input batch"

Refused, but by the decoder noticing rather than the door deciding, and the
sentence says what the frame is NOT. The frame is a picture. A rule that only
knows what a frame is not passes the next non-input the moment one is added.

There was no bounded inbound queue and no drop policy anywhere.

### What is now true

`frames.js` says of every type byte whether it decides anything. The map is
exhaustive - 17 entries, one per type this package has - and a byte missing
from it is refused by number rather than assumed harmless.

  0x01 RoundContract      0x08 InputBatch        0x0e FeeClaim
  0x02 EntryContract      0x09 Transcript        0x0f ServiceRecord
  0x03 Advert             0x0a CheckpointReceipt 0x10 DonationSet
  0x04 CensusLeaf         0x0b Objection
  0x05 Checkpoint         0x0c SlashProof        0x11 Ghost   PICTURE
  0x06 Result             0x0d SettlementRecord
  0x07 PayoutTable

`bearsAuthority(bytes, as)` refuses a ghost offered as an input, a receipt, a
census entry, a bond, an objection, a result or a payout table, and the reason
names the frame: "a Ghost is a picture and carries no authority, so it cannot
be an input". The node's door uses it, so the socket answers that instead of
"not an input batch", and an unused byte is refused as "no frame of this
protocol begins with 0x7f" rather than handed to the batch reader.

### The drop order, printed rather than asserted from memory

  queue in           : InputBatch, Ghost, Checkpoint, Ghost, CheckpointReceipt
  limit 4, new InputBatch
    DROPPED in order : Ghost, Ghost
    KEPT             : InputBatch, Checkpoint, CheckpointReceipt, InputBatch

  all-evidence queue, limit 3, new InputBatch
    DROPPED          : InputBatch   (the newcomer, not the evidence)
    KEPT             : Checkpoint, InputBatch, CheckpointReceipt

Pictures go, oldest first, and nothing else goes. IMPLEMENTATION section 7:
"above a threshold drop ghost frames first - they are non-authoritative by
definition - and never receipts." §11 says why it is not a preference:
"publishing is the client's duty, and unpublished inputs cost the player the
run", so a node that shed a batch to make room for a picture would be taking a
run away over rendering. With no picture left, the NEWCOMER is refused rather
than an accepted frame discarded - refusing the newcomer leaves the sender able
to publish it again, which is their duty anyway.

An unknown frame is NOT sheddable. Wrong in the safe direction: something this
package cannot name might be evidence.

### Mutants: 10 planted, 10 killed, none retracted

  (a) accept a ghost as an input or vote   ghost given authority: 4 red
                                           authority not checked:  1 red
                                           the node's door removed: 1 red
  (b) drop inputs before ghosts            anything droppable:      2 red
                                           nothing droppable:       2 red
                                           unknown frame sheddable: 1 red
                                           newest picture first:    1 red
                                           evidence shed for room:  1 red
  (c) let a ghost authorise a round        an unknown byte admitted: 1 red
                                           (the same door: a type nobody
                                           declared would reach `round.batch`)

The drop list not being reported also dies (2 red): a queue that shed silently
would be a queue whose order nobody could print.

### Suites

protocol 357/357 (was 353), core 83/83, blwp-node 71/71 (was 70), blwp-client
89/89, money guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean. No wire
format moved: `frames.js` reads type bytes that already existed.

### Still not this piece

No fan-out, no interest management, no renderer, no lobby. No Unity, no C#, no
PhysX, no collider. No ghost handed to `step` - the missing parameter from
piece 1 is untouched and its two mutants still die.

## M2.2 item 18, piece 3: which twenty others you see

IMPLEMENTATION section 7: "Ghost fan-out uses interest management: each
connection subscribes to ~20 others (nearest plus leaderboard top), recomputed
every few seconds - O(N.K), never O(N^2)."

### Measured before any code

  grep -i "subscri|fanout|fan-out|interest|nearest|broadcast"
  over blwp-node/src, blwp-client/src, protocol/src   ->  NOTHING

Greenfield. No subscription, no budget, no fan-out anywhere.

### The bandwidth claim, measured rather than asserted

  K = 20
   N   frames sent   everyone-sees-everyone   ratio
    2            2                      2      1.0
    5           20                     20      1.0
   10           90                     90      1.0
   20          380                    380      1.0
   40          800                   1560      1.9
   60         1200                   3540      3.0
  120         2400                  14280      6.0

Below the budget the two are equal, because there is nobody to leave out.
Above it, frames are exactly N.K and grow linearly while everyone-sees-everyone
grows with the square: doubling 60 to 120 doubles the frames and quadruples the
alternative.

### The half that matters more than bandwidth

A set a node chooses however it likes is a set the OPERATOR chooses: show a
player the competitors it wants them to see, hide the one about to beat them,
and the round looks different depending on which node answered. 0.9 lets a
player watch competitors "drive, struggle, fail and arrive"; it does not say
"watch whichever ones your node felt like sending".

So the rule is a pure function of the round's own state and TOTAL-ORDERED.
Every comparison ends in the entry id, so a tie is broken by something
intrinsic rather than by arrival order - the same fault a census tie on work
had before it was broken on the tip hash. Measured: the same twenty, in the
same ORDER, from a reversed input, from a rank-shuffled input, and from an
x-sorted input.

### K is NOT a contract field, and that is deliberate

The census depth and the committee size went onto the signed contract because
they decide who sits and what a bond is worth. A ghost decides nothing -
`frames.js` says so and the core has no argument one could arrive through - so
how many pictures a node can afford to send is that node's bandwidth policy,
not a rule the round signs. Naming it as `GHOST_SUBSCRIPTIONS = 20` keeps it
out of the round id AND out of an undeclared per-call argument.

### Distance is BigInt, and it has to be

The words are Q16.16 in an i32. Two trucks the same enormous distance away in
x, one a single unit further in z: exactly, one is nearer; as doubles they are
the same number, because the squared x is 2^62 and the ULP up there is 1024.
Tested with that fixture, and the mutant that computes the distance in Number
dies on it.

### Mutants: 11 planted, 11 killed, none retracted

no budget at all (4 red), the budget off by one (4), only leaders (1), only
neighbours (1), the leader half taking the whole budget (1), ties falling back
to arrival order (1), distance measured by x alone (1), distance in Number (1),
a player sent their own truck (3), leaders taken from the bottom of the board
(1), a negative budget accepted (1).

`compareBytes` was exported from `payout.js` rather than copied: a second
comparator is a second place for a total order to drift, the reason
`slotsForRole` imports 22A's pool mapping instead of restating it.

### Suites

protocol 362/362 (was 357), core 83/83, blwp-node 71/71, blwp-client 89/89,
money guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean. No wire format
moved: selection reads positions and ranks that a ghost frame already carries.

### What piece 3 does NOT include

The recompute cadence ("every few seconds") is a daemon's timer, not a rule -
nothing here schedules anything, and the function is called when a caller
decides to call it. No socket subscribes to anything yet; wiring the set into
the node's send loop needs the daemon that is parked. And piece 4 - the
renderer that must never carry a collider - is untouched: no Unity, no C#, no
PhysX.

## M2.2 item 18, piece 4: the renderer, and PhysX is given nothing to work with

0.9: "Other trucks are visible ghosts with no collision. Another player must
not be able to change my financial odds by ramming me, blocking a road,
pushing me, damaging me..." 0.10: "Alice's physics cannot change Bob's result."

The protocol already refuses to let a ghost be an input: its own type byte, no
authority (piece 2), and a core `step` with no argument one could arrive
through (piece 1). The remaining way a competitor could reach a run is through
the ENGINE - a ghost with a collider is a truck you can hit, a road you cannot
pass, a body your wheels climb.

### Measured first

The local truck is a real physics object: `CoreDrivenTruck` holds a Rigidbody
it switches to kinematic while the core drives, and WheelColliders under it.
So "ghosts do not collide" cannot be inherited from the scene having no
physics - the scene has plenty.

### What is now true

`GhostTruck` draws three numbers and carries nothing else. On Awake it strips
every Collider and Rigidbody in its hierarchy, with `DestroyImmediate` rather
than `Destroy`: Destroy runs at the end of the frame, so a ghost spawned and
stepped in the same frame would have had a live collider for exactly one
physics tick, which is all a collision needs. What it removed is COUNTED and
NAMED, so a prefab that keeps growing colliders shows up instead of being
quietly cleaned every frame.

The test fixture builds a ghost the way a careless prefab would - a
BoxCollider, a Rigidbody, and a SphereCollider on a child wheel - because a
rule that only held for objects which never had physics would hold for
nothing: a truck model arrives with colliders.

### The four PlayMode tests

  AGhostCarriesNoPhysicsAtAll          0 colliders, 0 rigidbodies, and the
                                       strip is reported: 2 colliders and 1
                                       body found and named
  OverlappingGhostsMoveTheTruckNot
    OneMillimetre                      two ghosts placed exactly on a real
                                       rigidbody truck, 60 fixed updates: 0
                                       collisions, position unmoved to 1e-4,
                                       velocity unchanged. THEN A CONTROL: the
                                       same cube WITH physics does collide, so
                                       the assertion is not measuring an engine
                                       that never collides at all
  AGhostCannotReachTheSimulation       no field or property of GhostTruck has
                                       the type BlwpCore, CoreDrivenTruck,
                                       TruckController or Rigidbody - the same
                                       structural argument the core makes about
                                       `step`'s parameter list
  AGhostStandsWhereTheFrameSays        Q16.16 in, metres out, negative and
                                       fractional words included, and showing a
                                       ghost never gives it physics back

### A test I broke, found by baselining rather than assuming

First PlayMode run: 220 total, 196 passed, 11 failed. Baseline with the two
files moved aside: 216 total, 193 passed, 10 failed. One MORE failure with my
change, and diffing the two result sets named it:

  PostOfficeTests.TheGogglesAnimate

Not a ghost test, and not a coincidence: my fixture is the only one in the
suite that runs PhysX on bodies of its own, it did 240 fixed updates, and it
left its cubes for TearDown. The goggles test watches a wall animate within two
wall-clock seconds, so it is the one a heavier neighbour tips over.

Fixed rather than listed: 120 fixed updates to 60 in each phase, and the
fixture destroys its own bodies at the end instead of leaving them. Second run:

### Auditing piece 4: a second door into the simulation, found and closed

Asked whether anything was still missing on the renderer, and compared the core
path against the old PhysX one again rather than from memory. One hole, and it
did not go through `step` at all.

`WorldSolids.Gather` scans EVERY BoxCollider in the scene and uploads the
qualifying ones into the core as boxes the truck cannot drive through. That is
a door into the simulation through `setSolids`, so piece 1's argument - "step
has no parameter a ghost could arrive through" - never sees it.

A ghost passes every exclusion `IsWorld` already had:

  not disabled          a ghost is active, it is being drawn
  not a trigger         a stray collider is a solid one
  not the yard layer    a ghost is on the map
  no attachedRigidbody  BECAUSE GhostTruck STRIPPED THE RIGIDBODY. The guard
                        that makes a ghost safe from PhysX is the same guard
                        that made it look like scenery here.
  not a child of the
    truck               it is a different truck

So a ghost that ever carried a BoxCollider - a streamed model, a prefab edit,
one careless AddComponent - would have been uploaded to the core as a wall.
0.9's "blocking a road", exactly.

TWO GUARDS, because one was not enough:

  1. `IsWorld` asks the COMPONENT: anything under a `GhostTruck` is not part of
     the solid world. Asked of the component rather than a name, a tag or a
     layer, because those are editable by somebody who does not know what they
     decide, and this one decides whether a player can wall another player in.
  2. `GhostTruck.OnTransformChildrenChanged` strips again whenever a child
     appears. Awake runs once, and this project STREAMS its truck model in -
     `ModelStreamer` parents it later, with whatever colliders its author gave
     it - so a ghost that only stripped at Awake would be clean for a second
     and solid afterwards.

## M2 late join: a run begins where the entry says it joined

### The spec, quoted rather than remembered

0.8: "A round supports a dynamically growing number of competitors... Late join
is a normal feature, not merely reconnect. Each accepted entrant receives the
same contract-defined mission duration `T_run`, even when wall-clock start
times differ."

Section 1: "All accepted players belong to the same logical round and payout
pool." Section 7: "Late joins simply add more Entry Contracts. The Round
Contract is never rewritten."

Section 6's timeline answers the committee question before it is asked:

  committee_time      beacon value appears -> committees selected & verified
                      |  ENTRY WINDOW OPENS HERE
  start_time          round begins for everyone committed so far
  entry_close_time    last late join

The committee is fixed BEFORE the entry window opens, so a late entrant cannot
grind a seed that was settled before they could enter. That is the spec's
answer, not a test's.

WHERE THE SPEC IS SILENT, and it is not invented here:

  - which TICK a late joiner starts at. The spec gives wall-clock times only.
    `joinTick` is this implementation's field.
  - how `entry_close_time` becomes a tick. That needs a protocol tick rate,
    which is parked. `entry_close_time` stays carried and unread.
  - what outcome a late arrival gets. No clause is specific to them; the
    nearest are section 14's ladder and "unstarted entries may ENTRY_VOID".
    Nothing was derived from that.

And a correction: PLAYER_LOST is not a term in this project. `payout.js` says
so - "PLAYER_LOST IS NOT A WORD HERE. FORFEIT already names the case". The
outcomes are DELIVERED, FAILED, FORFEIT, VOID, ENTRY_VOID.

### Measured before any code

  the entry says the player joined at tick 50
    a transcript beginning at tick  50 -> ACCEPTED, 9 ticks
    a transcript beginning at tick   0 -> ACCEPTED, 9 ticks
    a transcript beginning at tick 500 -> ACCEPTED, 9 ticks

  checkTranscript's only argument is the transcript. It never sees the entry.

The node DOES read `joinTick` - `round.js` `nextTick` returns it when an entry
has no ticks yet, so a late player's first batch is expected at 50. But the
verifier's own check, the one a replay depends on, had no such binding. A
player could publish a run that started before they joined, or one that skipped
four hundred ticks, and every protocol check passed.

### What is now true

`transcriptBelongsToEntry(transcript, entry)` refuses:

  a start before the join tick   "begins at tick 0 and that entry joined at 50"
  a start after it               "begins at tick 500 and that entry joined at 50"
  one tick either side           49 and 51 are both the wrong start
  another entry                  "a different entry than the transcript names"
  another round                  named separately
  no inputs at all               "carries no inputs, so there is nothing that
                                  began anywhere"

ITS OWN CHECK, not a fold into `checkTranscript`. The same run beginning at 0
still passes `checkTranscript` - it IS a chain, it simply is not this entry's -
and the test asserts that, so the new gate is doing the work rather than
riding on one that already refused.

### flatten, for a run that did not begin at zero

  a strike at absolute tick 54, run starting at 50 -> index 4
  firstTick 50, nine rows, first [65536, 50, 0, 0, 0]
  a gap inside a late run -> "expected tick 56, got 90"

That rebasing already existed and its own comment says why: "a transcript that
begins at tick 50 would otherwise put a strike at index 51 of a two-element
array - that is, nowhere - and the replay would be a different round with
nothing to say it had gone wrong." This letter pins it for the late case.

### Mutants: 8 planted, 8 killed, none retracted

start-tick check deleted, made "at or after", made "at or before", compared
against `batches[0].firstTick` instead of the entry's `joinTick` (the wrong
field - it would compare a value to itself), entry-id binding dropped, round
binding dropped, an empty transcript allowed to begin anywhere, and the run
length claimed as checked.

### What stays unchecked, named in the answer

The run LENGTH. 0.8's "same contract-defined mission duration `T_run`" needs
`player_run_duration`, which section 6 names and this Round Contract does not
carry - one of the eighteen absent names audited in item 16, parked because
adding one moves every round id. `transcriptBelongsToEntry` reports it rather
than assuming it.

guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean. PlayMode and EditMode

path - and `step` still takes one state and one player's five inputs.

### Closing out late join: the check nobody called, and a resume that began at zero

Asked whether item 19 was finished and found two things, both on this letter.

FIRST: `transcriptBelongsToEntry` was called by NOTHING outside its own tests.
That is the fault `censusRoot` had before item 15 - named by every contract and
read by no code - and a check nobody calls is a comment.

SECOND, and the reason it mattered. The node enforces the start tick on the way
IN: `round.batch` asks `nextTick`, which returns the entry's `joinTick` for a
first batch, and refuses "expected tick 50, got 0". Good, and pre-existing. But
the CLIENT's resume did this:

  this.nextTick = last ? batchTicks(last).at(-1) + 1 : 0;

That `: 0` is the reconnect of a player who joined at tick 50 and had not
published anything yet - a page reload between joining and the first batch.
They resumed numbering from zero, every batch after that carried the inputs of
one tick under the number of another, and the node would refuse them while the
page looked healthy.

  before   a fresh client resuming an entry that joined at 50  ->  nextTick 0
  after    the same client                                     ->  nextTick 50
  and an entry that joined at 0 still resumes at 0, so this reads the entry
  rather than adding a constant

THE ENTRY IS FETCHED AND THEN HASHED. An entry id is the hash of its bytes, so
`entryFor` refuses anything that does not hash to the id it asked for. 25.1's
rule for chain providers, applied to this one: a node may omit, and it may not
forge. And a fetched transcript now goes through `transcriptBelongsToEntry`, so
the check has a caller.

### A node that lies, because an honest one cannot test these

Two mutants survived at 0 red first - the entry not hashed, and the transcript
not checked against the entry - because the real node CANNOT produce the
answers those guards exist for: it enforces the start tick on ingest and always
returns the entry it was asked for. Testing a client's own checks against an
honest server measures nothing.

So the suite now stands up a small HTTP server that answers `/entry` with
somebody else's contract, and one that answers `/transcript` with a real,
correctly formed chain that simply begins at tick 0. Both are refused by name.
The control for the second is the first test in the file, against the REAL
node: a player who joined at 50 resumes at 50. It is not repeated against the
stub, because `resume` goes on to recover receipts and a stub answering those
would be a second node rather than a lying one.

### Mutants: 3 planted, 3 killed

resume falling back to tick zero; the fetched entry not hashed against the id;
a transcript not checked against the entry it names. Added to the 8 on the
protocol side: 11 for this letter, none retracted.

guard 12 files clean, determinism guard 19 files clean, client bundle rebuilt
(172.5 KB). PlayMode and EditMode not re-run: nothing in Unity moved.

                        Section 6 names it; this Round Contract does not carry

  entry_close_time      section 6's "last late join". Carried by every contract

## M2.2 item 20, first slice: the board, and it decides nothing

0.11: "Derived from signed final protocol results. It may show pseudonym, live
run status, delivered/failed state, score, rank, cargo statistics and payout.
THE LEADERBOARD IS PRESENTATION, NOT AUTHORITY."

### Measured before any code: what a signed final carries

`encodePlayerResult` is 168 bytes plus a 64-byte signature:

  roundId | playerPubkey | outcome | score | transcriptHash | simCoreHash
  | nodePubkey

Against 0.11's seven fields - THIS ACCOUNTS FOR 4 OF THE 7:

  delivered/failed  ON THE FINAL      `outcome`: DELIVERED, FAILED, FORFEIT, VOID
  score             ON THE FINAL      u32
  payout            DERIVABLE         `computePayoutTable`, section 20's
                                      F(contract, membership, results) - and
                                      NOT this slice's to compute
  rank              DERIVABLE         it IS the ordering, which is this slice
  pseudonym         NOT CARRIED       0.12: "clients MAY derive a friendly
                                      pseudonym" - a rendering of the player
                                      key, client-side, not a protocol field
  cargo statistics  NOT CARRIED       no field, and not derivable from a final
  live run status   IMPOSSIBLE HERE   a final is after the run. 0.11 lists it
                                      while also saying the board is derived
                                      from finals - a tension in the SPEC, not
                                      in this code, and not resolved by
                                      inventing a source. It would come from
                                      marks and ghosts, a different letter.

The three that cannot come from a final are RETURNED AS NAMED PARKED FIELDS,
not left as blank columns: a column nobody filled looks the same as a column
somebody forgot, and the first is a decision while the second is a bug.

### What is now true

`leaderboard(rows, { contract })` where a row is `{ result, signedBy }` - the
shape `provisionallyFinal` already takes.

  the committee is the ROUND's, off `contract.nodes`, not a list the caller
  brings. A caller who could choose the committee could choose which results
  counted as final, and the board is what a player reads to find out whether
  they won.

  a result the committee has not made final DOES NOT APPEAR. Not ranked last,
  not greyed: section 13's threshold is what makes a result a result, and
  showing the others would put a node's opinion beside a committee's decision
  as though they were the same kind of thing. Five signatures from OFF the
  committee are not five seats.

  order is score descending, then the player key. Never arrival. A stable sort
  keeps the INPUT order and the input order is exactly what must not decide a
  rank - the tie discipline the census needed on the tip hash and interest
  management needed on the entry id.

  A REFUND IS NOT A PLACE. Section 18: "VOID and ENTRY_VOID entries neither
  contribute to nor draw from the pool", so ranking one last would put a
  refunded player below one who lost and the board would say something the
  money does not. They are shown with `rank: null`. FORFEIT keeps its place:
  `isRefund` covers VOID and ENTRY_VOID and not FORFEIT, and the payout table
  puts a forfeit's stake into the loser pool - it played and lost.

  no money. The row keys are exactly playerPubkey, outcome, score, signers,
  rank, and a test refuses any key matching /payout|amount|msat|sat|prize|
  winnings/ - so a second scoring path cannot be added quietly.

### Measured

  four scores 900/700/500/100 in three shuffled orders -> identical rows and
    identical ranks every time
  three players tied on 700, offered forwards and backwards -> 0x33, 0x66,
    0x99 both times
  4 of 5 signatures -> excluded, "has not made that result final: 4 of 5"
  0 signatures     -> "nobody has signed a result"
  5 strangers      -> excluded, "came from elsewhere"
  VOID             -> rank null, after the ranked, and among themselves by key
  FORFEIT          -> rank 2 of 3, between a delivery and a failure

### Mutants: 12 planted, 12 killed, none retracted

The four required: ordering by arrival (2 red), ties unbroken (1), an
under-signed final admitted (1), VOID ranked (1). And eight more: the board
ordered upwards (2), four signatures enough (1), a stranger's signature
counting (1), FORFEIT losing its place (1), the unranked ordered by arrival
(1), ranks starting at zero (2), what a final cannot say not named (1), and
the board carrying an amount (1).

## M2.2 item 20, second slice: the standing an interest set uses is the board's

`interestSet` read `rank` straight off the object it was handed. That is the
fault removed five times before - from the census depth, the committee size,
the committee seed, the bond floor and the protocol version. A rank a caller
picks is a rank the OPERATOR picks: say the player about to overtake you is
nineteenth and they fall out of the twenty you are shown, with nothing forged
and nothing to notice.

### What is now true

`interestSet(viewer, others, { limit, board })`. `others` carry a
`playerPubkey`; the standing is looked up on the BOARD by that key, and a
`rank` written on the caller's object is IGNORED - the treatment RESOLVE gives
a census entry's claimed roles and key, because the object is somebody's
summary and the signed thing beside it is what counts.

  the real leaders demoted to 900+ and the stragglers promoted to 0 on the
    caller's own objects   ->  the same set, unchanged
  no board at all          ->  no leaders at all; the whole budget goes to the
                               nearest, because nobody has a standing to be a
                               leader by

SOMEBODY STILL DRIVING HAS NO STANDING, and that is not a gap. A board is built
from results the committee has made final; mid-round most players have none.
They are watchable as neighbours and join the leaders half when their result is
final - and late join is why finals arrive DURING a round at all, since each
entrant gets T_run from their own start and they finish at different moments.

A REFUND IS NOT A STANDING either. The board shows it unranked, and unranked is
not a place.

### Mutants: 6 planted, 6 killed

Two survived at 0 red first, and both were fixtures that could not tell the
answers apart:

  a refund counts as a standing     the refunded players were placed NEAR, so
                                    the nearest half took them anyway and a
                                    leaders half that mistook `rank: null` for
                                    a standing looked identical. They are far
                                    away now and the unranked four are close,
                                    so the two halves disagree about them.
  the standing is keyed by entry,
    not by player                   every fixture used the same bytes for
                                    `entryId` and `playerPubkey`, so a lookup
                                    on either found the same row. They differ
                                    now, and the board's number one is placed
                                    FARTHEST away - a correct lookup gives it
                                    the leaders seat, a wrong one leaves the
                                    leaders half empty and the top of the board
                                    disappears.

The board fixture is built by calling `leaderboard` on real signed finals
rather than writing rank numbers by hand: hand-written ranks would test this
file against itself, and the point of the slice is that ONE ordering is
computed the same way everywhere.

TWO GAPS, both closed on the same slice.

by PLAYER and a subscription keys by ENTRY; they are different namespaces, and

  an other with NO playerPubkey, on a board ranking its entryId bytes
    before  ->  [5, 6]   the keyless truck took the leaders seat
    after   ->  [6, 7]   the seats go to the nearest, and the same truck WITH

  mutants   2 planted, 2 killed, 1 retracted with the code simplified
  protocol  375 -> 377

### The board's cost per broadcast, named not fixed

`standings(board)` rebuilds its map inside every `interestSet` call, so a
`fanOut` over N viewers rebuilds it N times - O(N.B) where B is the board. It
is correct and it is not free. Not changed here: the shape that fixes it is
hoisting the map into `fanOut`, which is a different slice and would be
measured against a real N rather than guessed at.

## M2.2 item 20, third slice: the payout on each row is the table's

Section 20 makes the payout table `F(contract, membership, results)`, and 0.11
makes the board presentation. A second thing that produced amounts would be a
second scoring path.

### The board is not handed a table

There is no argument for one. It is handed the INPUTS - the entries with their
stakes and outcomes - and calls `computePayoutTable`, the one implementation.
A forged table cannot be passed because there is nowhere to pass it, which is
the same shape as the core's missing ghost parameter: the guarantee is the
absence, not a check.

AND THE INPUTS MUST BE THIS ROUND'S. Every payout entry is measured against the
final the board already accepted:

  a player the committee made no final for   "counts a player the committee has
                                              made no result final for"
  FAILED promoted to DELIVERED               "says DELIVERED for a player whose
                                              final result is FAILED"
  a score inflated to 9999                   "scores a player 9999 where the
                                              final says 800"
  an amountMsat written on the input          ignored - the board reads the
                                              table it computed, exactly as an
                                              injected rank is ignored

### Zero is a paid amount

The table lists everybody activated, and a qualifier who places outside the
paying ranks is paid 0n. A player the table does not list at all - a refunded
run, which section 18 says neither contributes nor draws - has NO `payoutMsat`
field. Measured both ways in one board: the loser carries `payoutMsat: 0n` and
`'payoutMsat' in row` is true; the refunded player has no such key.

### Payout is a column, not a sort key

The order was settled by score then player key; money must not move anybody.
The mutant that sorted by amount survived at first because the fixture's payout
order agreed with its score order - the fourth time this letter a fixture could
not tell two answers apart. It is measured on a CROSSED pair now: a FAILED run
with the highest score is ranked first and paid nothing, while a lower-scoring
delivery is ranked second and paid.

the board computing an amount itself (2 red), an amount read off the caller's
object (3), a player the table omits paid zero (1), a payout entry not matched
to the final outcome (1) or the final score (1), a player with no final paid
(1), and payout used as a sort key (1).

## M2.2 item 20, fourth slice: the board says what it did not check

### The bookkeeping first

PRIORITIES said of slice 1 "and no column carries money" while slice 3, two
sentences later, said each row carries the payout. A working list that
contradicts itself in adjacent sentences is read at the top of every turn.
Removed.

### The hole

`provisionallyFinal` counts `{ resultId, nodePubkey }` pairs against the
round's committee. It does NOT verify a signature, and `result.js` says why:
"this package carries no curve, so the caller passes what it has checked."
That boundary is right.

What was wrong is that the BOARD did not say so. Five entries in an array were
counted as five committee signatures and the answer came back looking exactly
like a verified one. Every other door names its curve boundary - `resolveCensus`
returns "advertisement signature (no curve in this package)", `acceptAdvert`
the same, `provesEquivocation` takes its verify from the caller - and the one
place that decides whether a row APPEARS was silent about it.

### Measured, before and after

  BEFORE, unchecked: 3 entries
    1. pseudonym
    2. cargo statistics
    3. live run status

  AFTER, unverified: 4 entries
    1. committee signatures      <- "counted against the round's committee,
                                     not verified: no curve in this package,
                                     so a caller passes what it has checked"
    2. pseudonym
    3. cargo statistics
    4. live run status

  AFTER, caller says it verified: 3 entries, the notice gone

  rows identical: true

`signaturesVerified` is a claim about the CALLER's own work, not about the
data, so it moves the report and nothing else: same rows, same order, same
ranks, same payouts, same exclusions. Asserted with payouts in play as well as
without. A caller that lies there has lied to itself.

the notice dropped (2 red), the notice always present regardless of the claim
(1), the claim inverted (2), the notice reduced to the word "signatures" (2),
and the claim moving a row rather than only the report (1).

The board already REFUSED these three; it did not say who owed them. Measured

The foreign player is ABSENT, not paid nothing: a payout that counts them is
