      "The transaction had an invalid input: 0-The preimage is invalid"; both

   B5 a second spend of the redeemed lock 1:
      "The transaction had an invalid input: 0-No contract found for given
      ContractId"

M3, FROST/DKG SLICE STILL OPEN: MEASURED ROGUE-KEY ATTACK ON A 2-OF-2 DKG (no proof of knowledge)
  TEST              blwp-node/test/dkg-rogue.test.js (records today's facts and
                    asserts them; flips to "refused" when the proof lands).
                    Construction: the dishonest seat takes the honest A0 it was
                    sent, publishes A0' = X - A0_honest for a key X it owns
                    (never knowing A0''s secret), picks the honest seat's share
                    r, and solves A1' = (rG - A0') / j_honest as a POINT, so the
                    honest share lies on the published polynomial.
  PROTOCOL FACTS    acceptContribution: accepts | honest share (openMyContribution)
                    still verifies | combineShares emits the attacker's X as the
                    group key | the attacker ALONE signs a BIP-340 signature that
                    verifies under the group key. All four true.
  DAEMON ORDER      (real honest daemon, dishonest peer on its own socket, logged)
                    1 honest dkg.run starts and DEALS
                    2 honest POSTs its contribution to the peer - the peer holds
                      the honest A0 and has dealt nothing
                    3 honest GETs the peer's contribution -> 404
                    4 run() returns ok=false: "1 of the committee's 2 seats have
                      contributed"
                    5 peer POSTs the rogue contribution -> 201 taken
                    6 honest finish() ok=true, group key = the attacker's X
                    and the pool's output key (poolOutput) is spendable by the
                    attacker alone. GET /dkg serves a node's own contribution to
                    any caller; POST /dkg takes a committee member's any time.
  WHY IT WORKS      Feldman checks only that each honest share lies on the
                    published polynomial; with honest seats < threshold (2-of-2:
                    one honest seat) the dealer can fix those shares and solve
                    the remaining commitments as points. combineShares guards
                    one-contribution-per-seat, not dealing last.

  READING           One bad share locks the round's payout for good: the asker
                    (and every honest seat that signed) refuses any second list.
                    That rule is right about nonces - reusing one nonce pair
                    under two lists leaks the share - so the fix is not to drop
                    it but to retry with FRESH nonces, never the spent ones. And
                    naming the cheater needs each seat's public share, computable
                    from the DKG commitments every seat already stores.
  NEXT              verify the aggregate before anything is written or sent; on
                    failure verify each share against that seat's public share
                    (even-normalised, pool-tweaked), name the cheater, discard
                    the spent nonces, retry with fresh ones and a set without it.

M3, NIP-04: A KEY THE ENVELOPE WAS NOT SEALED TO - MEASURED BEFORE
  LINE              PRIORITIES: "client wallet-nwc's 'a third key opened an
                    envelope' flakes about 1 in 256 (NIP-04 has no MAC)".
  TEST              blwp-client/test/nip04-stranger.test.js: one envelope
                    ("pay_invoice") sealed between two fixed keys, opened with
                    4096 stranger keys; every key and the iv from sha256 of a
                    counter, so the count is exact and repeatable.
  FACTS             15 of 4096 strangers "opened" it (1 in 273): nip04Decrypt
                    returned ok with garbage full of U+FFFD - AES-CBC passed the
                    padding check and the decode was non-fatal. 0 saw the
                    message.
  READING           NIP-04's content is a UTF-8 string; bytes that are not UTF-8
                    are not a NIP-04 message, and the decrypt said they were.
                    Not the gap, found beside it: nwcCall does not check that an
                    answer event is signed by the wallet's key or names the
                    request (NIP-01) - it trusts the relay's authors filter.

M3, NIP-04: FIXED - A KEY THE ENVELOPE WAS NOT SEALED TO OPENS NOTHING
  CHANGE            blwp-client nwc.js nip04Decrypt decodes the plaintext
                    strictly (TextDecoder fatal): a NIP-04 message is text, so
                    bytes that are not UTF-8 are refused ("that answer is not
                    text, so it was not sealed to this key"), not replaced.
  FACTS (after)     same 4096 deterministic stranger keys: 0 opened (was 15),
                    0 saw the message; the pair still opens it to "pay_invoice".
                    wallet-nwc 24/24 with its random-stranger assertion as it
                    was. The residue is not zero in principle - a stranger's
                    garbage must pass the padding check AND be valid UTF-8 -
                    but it is no longer 1 in 256; 0 in 4096 here.
  MUTANT            the decode made non-fatal again -> 15 opened, the test red.
  FOUND, NOT THIS   nwcCall takes any EVENT frame the relay sends: it does not
                    check that the answer is signed by the wallet's key, that
                    its id is its own hash, or that it names the request
                    (NIP-01); it trusts the relay's authors filter. The shared
                    secret still binds the content.
  COUNTS STOOD ON   protocol 487/487, node 531/531 (sequential chunks, 0
                    cancelled), client 247/247. No Unity/WebGL (not on the page).

M3 W5 STEP 1: THE SEATS MAKE THE ROUND'S CLAIM KEY
  WHY FIRST         W5b's forfeit is a threshold signature by the round's claim
                    key, and every lock rehearsal (W1a, W1b) had handed the seats
                    that key (claimKeyFor, keys.json). Measured before anything:
                    does a round the daemons seat themselves have one?
  BEFORE            fresh Daily 2-of-2 (standUpRound), nothing injected: neither
                    seat held a group key ("this node has no share of that
                    committee's key yet"), /claim-key 409 and 409; dkg.run by
                    hand, twice on both: "1 of the committee's 2 seats have
                    contributed". So on a daemon-seated round the page counted 0
                    of 2 and would lock nothing: W1b's shipping path rested on
                    the injected key.
  CAUSE             nothing in server.js or main.js ran the key generation; its
                    peers were a daemon-wide list, [] on a launched daemon (the
                    tests set dkg.peers by hand); and once the peers were given,
                    Dkg.finish still asked the daemon-wide list for the other
                    seats' agreements ("1 of the committee's 2 seats have said
                    which contributions they combined").
  FIX               a seat that seats a round from its census runs its half of
                    the key generation with the round's own committee endpoints
                    (endpointsOf, the rule the verify and payout paths use), and
                    again every second until the key exists (at least 30 runs,
                    while entries are open); Dkg.run and Dkg.finish take those
                    peers. No key is injected and no peer wired by hand; a
                    harness that hands claimKeyFor makes none (and is labelled
                    HARNESS KEY where a test still does).
  TIMED             paying lock round: seat B held the key 266 ms after the round
                    was up, seat A at 1582 ms (a second run); free round: 300 and
                    305 ms. The same group key on both.
  THE PAGE          opened on the link at once, it counted "1 of 2" and refused
                    the seat (measured). It now asks again every second for up
                    to 30 s (awaitAttestedClaimKey), saying the count; nothing
                    short of the threshold is ever accepted (claim-key-wait.test).
  AFTER             claim-key-own.test.js (shipping path, nothing injected): key
                    made in 322-331 ms, both seats one 33-byte group key,
                    /claim-key 200 200 serving it, the page 2 of 2 on it.
                    Mutant (no seat-time run): red, 409 409, 0 attested.
                    Page rehearsal, fresh federation, no key injected: the page
                    locked at c81dad3e025428403b3a0f53d7942a78455baaf177b4fe7483a2bf982348aeff:0,
                    the federation holds it (146 blocks left), /entry 201 201,
                    /lock 201 201, both seats committed 980000 msat; after PLAY
                    32/29 batches, 4/4 receipts, none refused; the no-lock mutant
                    was refused and not seated.
  NOT DONE          the seat that restarts mid key generation restarts it only
                    when the round is posted again; rounds larger than 2-of-2
                    make the key over contract.nodes, which claimKeyOf already
                    reads (measured here only on 2 of 2).

  SLICE             W5b (PRIORITIES): §23.2's first row - "DELIVERED (qualifying):
                    forfeit the stake lock -> it returns to the player's key;
                    threshold settlement signature over the lock, published; the
                    player's own client redeems it, and only the player can".
  TODAY (read)      a seat forfeits a verified lock: NO - the node's only cancel
                    is the Lightning hold invoice's (lnd-port, custody). A FROST
                    signature over a lock's contract id at any door: NO - the only
                    daemon FROST is PoolSigning, which signs taproot sighashes of
                    pool spends it rebuilt, under the TWEAKED pool key; a forfeit
                    is an untweaked BIP-340 signature by claim_pk over the
                    contract id. The page verifies and redeems: NO - the wasm lock
                    client has refund, not the Cancel(sig) witness (only the
                    native rehearsal tool's redeem has it).
  HOLES, AS RULED   (a) VOID: protocol names VOID/ENTRY_VOID and no node code
                    produces either (replay.js: "cannot be"); §16's ENTRY_VOID is
                    unbuilt, the result window's VOID parked. Out of W5b; ENTRY_VOID
                    (§16) is the next unblocked item. No Void is recorded by hand.
                    (b) "qualifying" is DELIVERED and score >= min_score (§18);
                    preimage.js has qualifies = outcome === 'DELIVERED' - fixed in
                    W5b. A Delivered run below min_score gets no forfeit; its lock
                    takes the default refund at expiry. (c) nothing claims a
                    loser's lock until W4 (parked behind the fee-lock ruling): a
                    loser refunds at expiry and loses only fees until then. A
                    loser's forfeit request is 409 and the lock stays held.
  THE RULE          PoolSigning's: a seat signs only a forfeit it rebuilt from its
                    own verified lock record, only when its own finality says the
                    run qualifies and is final with the window closed; nonces in
                    memory, one message per nonce pair; the seats exchange
                    commitments and shares; the combined signature at a public
                    door.
  HARNESS           a delivering run under the round's real randomness: a world
                    secret searched with the core's own replay (harness work,
                    labelled); a short objection window through the round's own
                    objectionWindowMs.

M3 W5b PIECE 1: THE SEATS FORFEIT A QUALIFIER'S LOCK, AND ONLY A QUALIFIER'S
  BUILT             blwp-node/src/forfeit.js: a seat rebuilds the forfeit's
                    message - the lock's contract id - from the lock IT verified
                    (the federation port hashes it), and signs only when its own
                    finality says FINAL (window closed) and its own result
                    qualifies (protocol isQualifier: DELIVERED and score >=
                    min_score, now one rule for the payout table, preimage.js and
                    the forfeit). One nonce pair per message, in memory; one share
                    per commitment list. Doors: POST /forfeit-commit,
                    /forfeit-share, /forfeit-signature (between seats); GET
                    /forfeit (public). Each seat keeps the combined signature
                    (forfeits table) - its record that it released the stake.
  FOUND             a seat that reaches no Lightning (a lock round's) stopped its
                    finality watch after one pass: settleTheStakes returned
                    before computing what was waiting, so the seat that posted
                    first never gathered the other's posting - "1 of 2
                    settlement seats have posted", never FINAL (measured: both
                    forfeit tests timed out at 20 s). It now hands back what is
                    waiting and keeps posting and gathering until FINAL, as a
                    Lightning seat always did.
  MEASURED          forfeit.test.js (two in-process seats, the claim key's
                    generation started by hand - labelled; the shipping path is
                    claim-key-own.test.js):
                      before the close          409 "no forfeit before the result is final"

                                                under the round's claim key; verifies
                                                (BIP-340); seat B keeps and serves the same
                      loser (FAILED, score 128) 409 "not a qualifier"; kept by 0 seats;
                                                its lock still held
                      Delivered, score 12,      409 "not a qualifier" (min_score 100)
                      below min_score
                      one seat's share alone    does not verify under the claim key
                    MUTANTS: the qualifier refusal removed -> the loser's forfeit
                    200 and kept by 2 seats, 2 of 2 tests red; the watch's early
                    return restored -> 1 of 2 tests red (the other reached FINAL

                    key"; B's /entry-void 404; B holds no mark; B's round open.

                    held and no key opens it before expiry. A seat that really holds
                    the player's signed first mark can still close it early and push
                    "closed" - a 2-of-2 veto, which either seat always has by
                    withholding receipts - and the forfeit then pays only the
                    player's refund key: not a stranger, not a seat.

M3.3-34 ENTRY_VOID PIECE: THE WALK-AWAY (§15), READ AND MEASURED - NO CODE CHANGED (2026-09-12)
  THE SPEC (multiplayer_p2p.md, header "BLWP v4.6")
    §15 Disconnect rule: "After stake commitment: A transcript that stops becomes
        a deterministic result. Missing inputs follow the neutral-input policy; if
        checkpoints stop beyond tolerance, the valid run ends at the last receipted
        checkpoint; replay determines the final state; the player normally becomes
        FAILED or FORFEIT. Closing the browser does not escape a losing stake."
    §16: "Before stake commitment: no financial entry exists; no loss." ENTRY_VOID
        only "after commitment, before the first financial tick" when fewer than the
        threshold of game/verify seats are available - a seat outage, not a player.
    §13C: VOID only when no result reaches quorum and the fault is the operator's.
    §14: VOID / ENTRY_VOID reachable only from PROVISIONAL.
    In a player's words: once your stake is committed, walking away is not a
    refund - the round replays what you sent and you normally lose (FAILED or
    FORFEIT); only the seats failing you before your first tick refunds you
    (ENTRY_VOID), or the committee failing to agree (VOID). PLAYER_LOST is not an
    outcome in the spec or the code (DELIVERED, FAILED, FORFEIT, VOID, ENTRY_VOID).
    NOT DEFINED ANYWHERE: "neutral-input policy" and "tolerance" appear only in
    §15's sentence (lines 1754-1755). No old C# path exists (no disconnect, idle
    or neutral-input code in unity-proto/Assets/Scripts): intent is §15 alone.
  MEASURED TODAY    tools/no-mark-probe.mjs, two in-process seats (the
                    closed-claim harness), deadline 900, both seats close:
    (A) paid, seated (entry, handout, lock 201 at both), sends nothing:
        both seats' replay "that transcript carries no ticks" - no result;
        no ENTRY_VOID, no FORFEIT; /forfeit 409 "0 of 2 agree on any one run";
        lock held, expiry 1200 > height 1000 -> the player's key refunds it.
    (B) paid, first mark at tick 60 (receipted at both), then nothing:
        both "that run is still LIVE at its last stored tick, so it came to
        nothing yet" (verdict.js resultFrom) - no result; the same refund at expiry.
    (C) free, seated, sends nothing: "that transcript carries no ticks" - no result.
    What the other seat and the operator see: a seated entry with no result,
    no record, no board row; the money path does nothing and the lock expires
    back to the player. "Closing the browser does not escape a losing stake" is
    not true today - before the first mark or after it.
  THE GAP           the no-first-mark walk-away accounts for 1 of the 2 ways a
                    stopped transcript ends with no result today (nothing sent;
                    LIVE at the last receipted mark). Both miss the same rule:
                    §15's "ends at the last receipted checkpoint ... becomes a
                    deterministic result" is not built - the receipted prefix
                    exists (canonicalTranscript), the ending of it does not. And
                    2 of §15's terms have no definition to build to.
  SMALLEST CHANGE   (needs two rulings first, not invented here)
                    1. tolerance: which silence counts as "stopped" - proposed:
                       the round's start deadline for the first mark (900 ticks,
                       the rule seats already enforce), the round's close for a
                       later mark.
                    2. the outcome of a run ended that way: FAILED (it did not
                       deliver) or FORFEIT (as the late start already is) for no

                    Then, in protocol (a rule beside first-mark.js) and the node's
                    close (verify/verdict): past tolerance, a run with no receipted
                    mark, or LIVE at its last one, is signed with the ruled outcome

M3.3-34 THE WALK-AWAY CLOSE (§15): NO FIRST MARK IS FORFEIT, A STOPPED RUN IS FAILED (2026-09-12)
  RULED             (Daniel) walking away after a seat is taken is not ENTRY_VOID and
                    not VOID. Tolerance: a missing first mark is stopped when the
                    round's start deadline (900 ticks) passes with no receipted mark;
                    a run with marks is stopped when checkpoints cease before the
                    round's close, and ends at its last receipted checkpoint.
                    Outcomes: no first mark = FORFEIT, score 0, empty receipted
                    transcript (the late start's family); a mid-run stop = FAILED
                    at the last receipted checkpoint. No PLAYER_LOST; core
                    unchanged; neutral input is not a sim rule this turn; no W4.

M3.3-34 ONE SEAT REFUSED: §13C'S VOID AFTER THE RESULT WINDOW (2026-09-12)
  RULED             (Daniel) a seated entry whose on-time first mark is receipted
                    below the threshold, every seat it is short of having been up
                    and REFUSED it: both seats HOLD until the result window has
                    passed (not at the close), then record explicit VOID - final,
                    not HOLDING; the lock held (no act: it returns at its expiry),
                    forfeit door 409, out of the pool and the payout table; Daily
                    stake 0: recorded VOID only. The refusing seat holding a
                    different first mark: FORFEIT. Unanswered / down: ENTRY_VOID,
                    unchanged. A seat unreachable at the close: hold, no VOID. A
                    refusal made good in time: 2 of 2, the run's own outcome. A
                    FINAL result is never voided. No live fault injection: a live
                    Daily refusal is a named gap.
  LAW               §13C: no result at the threshold after the result window -
                    proven equivocation -> FORFEIT, otherwise the operator side's
                    fault -> VOID, "refunded by letting the HTLC expire ...
                    excluded from the pool and from the payout table". §23.2:
                    VOID = do nothing. §14: VOID only from PROVISIONAL. Protocol
                    payout.js noQuorumOutcome / settlementAction already said so;
                    nothing in blwp-node called it.

M3.2 ITEM 6e: SHARES UNDER 1000 MSAT, RULED (Daniel 2026-09-13)
  The signed set is the allocation: floor-msat split, kept. No folding dust into the
  other recipient, no raised donation minimum, no share rewritten in the protocol. A
  2% donor on a 100000 msat stake is owed 1334/666; the 666 NO_ROUTE is lnd's default
  min_htlc, not a bind bug. The client reports that share unpaid and sends its msat
  nowhere - not the operator, not the other recipient; the player keeps what Lightning
  will not carry. The 5% pair (3334 + 1666 SETTLED) is the proof both recipients work
  on a paid local round. Closed.

                    HELD; an entry that ends ENTRY_VOID (or a round that goes VOID) does
                    not get its donation back, and nothing here refunds it.

                    fee rule, the payout table, payout-spend, invoiceMatchesEntry and
                    the page's quote line (nwc.js owedLine). TWO places subtracted by
                    hand, stake less fee with NO donation: server.js /federation-invoice

                    20000" - a donor seated who could never pay.
  THE FIX (4a07f31) both read netStakeMsat; the page names its donation with
                    &donation= (msat; none is 0, and the client sends none for 0). An
                    unreadable donation (-1, 1.5, abc, 0x10) or one the stake cannot hold

                    stake lock, page-lock.js:99, already netStakeMsat).
  ALSO CHECKED      the spend log: a donation share is never marked returned (only a
                    stake is), so a winner who donated keeps the share as spent and a
                    voided entry's donation stays spent (no refund on void, ruled).
                    Preflight sizes the largest hold with donation 0 - an upper bound,
